fields.overview_heading: A hospital facing coordination challenges across departments
fields.overview_content:
Universal Hospital provides diagnostic, treatment, surgical, chemotherapy and transplant services across multiple departments. Its infrastructure includes critical care units, CT/MRI facilities, an in-house blood bank, a cath lab and a modular operation theatre for transplant procedures.

These services require teams to share patient information and work across departments. Paper-based documentation and disconnected departmental systems made information harder to access, while surgical teams manually tracked OT schedules, pre-operative approvals and post-operative updates. These processes created delays and made it harder for teams to work efficiently.
fields.problem_heading: Four operational gaps affecting hospital care

problems.title: Paper-heavy documentation
problems.text: Staff relied on paper records and manual documentation, increasing administrative work and physical record storage. Doctors also spent more time managing records.

problems.title: Disconnected departmental systems
problems.text: Departments used separate software, leaving patient information scattered across systems. Duplicate entries and delayed updates made patient history harder to access.

problems.title: Manual surgical coordination
problems.text: OT schedules, pre-operative approvals and post-operative updates were handled manually. This made it harder for surgical teams to keep procedures and related updates aligned.

problems.title: Manual patient onboarding
problems.text: Patient registration involved manual data entry and verification, adding extra steps before patients could proceed with care.

fields.decision_intro: Universal Hospital needed a more integrated way to manage its clinical and administrative workflows. The hospital chose Healthray to connect patient records, laboratory, imaging, pharmacy and billing workflows in one system.
fields.quote_text: Morning OPD is usually very busy, so the system needs to be fast. I need old consultations, reports and medicines quickly while seeing the patient. Healthray shows all this on one screen, and even when lab or pharmacy updates come in, they reflect in the same patient record, so I don’t have to ask staff for old files. It saves my time during consultation.
fields.solution_heading: How Healthray helped Universal improve hospital workflows

solutions.title: Electronic Medical Records (EMR)
solutions.text: The information about patients was transferred from paper-based charting into EMR processes, providing quicker access to patients' medical history, lab results, and diagnostic imaging.

solutions.title: Integrated Hospital Information
solutions.text: Information from different departments was brought into a shared system, reducing duplicate entries and making updated patient information easier for teams to access.

solutions.title: Surgical Management
solutions.text: OT schedules, pre-operative approvals and post-operative updates were managed through a connected workflow, helping surgical teams coordinate these activities more effectively.

solutions.title: Digital Patient Onboarding
solutions.text: Digital forms and automated verification were introduced into the registration workflow, reducing manual steps.

fields.setup_heading: From data migration to team adoption
fields.setup_intro: Universal worked closely with the Healthray implementation team to transition its hospital operations to the new system.

steps.title: Existing data transferred
steps.text: Universal’s existing data was migrated to Healthray.

steps.title: Departments connected
steps.text: Clinical and administrative workflows were brought into one connected system.

steps.title: Staff trained
steps.text: Teams were trained on the configured workflows for daily use.

fields.results_intro: Universal's implementation of Healthray led to measurable improvements in patient flow, onboarding, clinical efficiency and record management.

results.title: reduction in paper usage
results.text: Switching to digital record-keeping brought down the usage of paper in terms of quantity from 2,000 sheets per day to 200 sheets, which is a 90% saving in terms of cost that comes to ₹8 lakh per year.

results.title: higher clinical efficiency
results.text: Unified medical records and faster access to clinical information contributed to a 25% increase in clinical efficiency.

results.title: shorter patient wait times
results.text: Healthray streamlined patient intake and coordination between departments, resulting in 45% shorter patient wait times.

results.title: faster patient onboarding
results.text: Digital forms and automated verification reduced manual steps, making patient onboarding 30% faster.
